sanskrit: tato gajaśiśuprakhyair upalaiḥ śailavāsinaḥ udyatair yuyudhānasya sthitā maraṇakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Then the mountain-dwellers, taking up boulders as large as young elephants, stood facing Yuyudhāna, longing for death.

sanskrit: kṣepaṇīyais tathāpy anye sātvatasya vadhaiṣiṇaḥ coditās tava putreṇa rurudhuḥ sarvatodiśam
english: Others too, hurling missiles and seeking the death of the Sātvata, urged on by your son, hemmed him in from every side.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatām eva śilāyuddhaṃ cikīrṣatām sātyakiḥ pratisaṃdhāya triṃśataṃ prāhiṇoc charān
english: As they rushed upon him, eager to wage war with stones, Sātyaki took aim and let fly thirty arrows.

sanskrit: tām aśmavṛṣṭiṃ tumulāṃ pārvatīyaiḥ samīritām bibhedoragasaṃkāśair nārācaiḥ śinipuṃgavaḥ
english: That tumultuous rain of stones, loosed by the mountaineers, the bull of Śini's line shattered with iron shafts like serpents.

sanskrit: tair aśmacūrṇair dīpyadbhiḥ khadyotānām iva vrajaiḥ prāyaḥ sainyāny avadhyanta hāhābhūtāni māriṣa
english: By the splinters of stone, blazing like swarms of fireflies, the troops for the most part were struck down, crying out in dismay, O honored one.

sanskrit: tataḥ pañcaśatāḥ śūrāḥ samudyatamahāśilāḥ nikṛttabāhavo rājan nipetur dharaṇītale
english: Then five hundred warriors, their great stones raised aloft, their arms severed, O king, fell to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: pāṣāṇayodhinaḥ śūrān yatamānān avasthitān avadhīd bahusāhasrāṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: He slew many thousands of those stone-fighting warriors who stood their ground and struggled on; and that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar bastamukhair aśmavṛṣṭiṃ samantataḥ ayohastaiḥ śūlahastair daradaiḥ khaśataṅgaṇaiḥ
english: Then once more, on every side, a rain of stones was cast by the goat-faced ones, by the Ayohastas, the spear-wielders, the Daradas, and the throngs of Khaśas.

sanskrit: ambaṣṭhaiś ca kuṇindaiś ca kṣiptāṃ kṣiptāṃ sa sātyakiḥ nārācaiḥ prativivyādha prekṣamāṇo mahābalaḥ
english: As the Ambaṣṭhas and the Kuṇindas hurled them again and again, the mighty Sātyaki, watching keenly, pierced each in turn with iron arrows.

sanskrit: adrīṇāṃ bhidyamānānām antarikṣe śitaiḥ śaraiḥ śabdena prādravan rājan gajāśvarathapattayaḥ
english: As the boulders were split in mid-air by his sharp arrows, at that din, O king, the elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers fled.

sanskrit: aśmacūrṇaiḥ samākīrṇā manuṣyāś ca vayāṃsi ca nāśaknuvann avasthātuṃ bhramarair iva daṃśitāḥ
english: Covered over with stone-dust, both men and birds were unable to hold their ground, as though stung by bees.

sanskrit: hataśiṣṭā virudhirā bhinnamastakapiṇḍikāḥ kuñjarāḥ saṃnyavartanta yuyudhānarathaṃ prathi
english: The elephants that survived the slaughter, streaming blood, their temple-bosses split open, turned away from the path of Yuyudhāna's chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdaḥ samabhavat tava sainyasya māriṣa mādhavenārdyamānasya sāgarasyeva dāruṇaḥ
english: Then there arose from your army, tormented by the Mādhava, a din terrible as the roar of the ocean, O honored one.

sanskrit: taṃ śabdaṃ tumulaṃ śrutvā droṇo yantāram abravīt eṣa sūta raṇe kruddhaḥ sātvatānāṃ mahārathaḥ
english: Hearing that tumultuous din, Droṇa said to his charioteer: "Yonder, O charioteer, is the wrathful great warrior of the Sātvatas in battle.

sanskrit: dārayan bahudhā sainyaṃ raṇe carati kālavat yatraiṣa śabdas tumulas tatra sūta rathaṃ naya
english: Rending the host in many places, he ranges over the field like Death itself. Where that tumultuous din is heard, there, O charioteer, drive the chariot.

sanskrit: pāṣāṇayodhibhir nūnaṃ yuyudhānaḥ samāgataḥ tathā hi rathinaḥ sarve hriyante vidrutair hayaiḥ
english: Surely Yuyudhāna has clashed with the stone-fighters, for all our chariot-warriors are being borne away by their bolting horses.

sanskrit: viśastrakavacā rugṇās tatra tatra patanti ca na śaknuvanti yantāraḥ saṃyantuṃ tumule hayān
english: Stripped of weapons and armor, shattered, they fall here and there, and the drivers cannot rein in their horses amid the tumult."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ bruvato rājan bhāradvājasya dhīmataḥ pratyuvāca tato yantā droṇaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ varam
english: As the wise son of Bharadvāja spoke thus, O king, the charioteer then answered Droṇa, foremost of weapon-bearers:

sanskrit: āyuṣman dravate sainyaṃ kauraveyaṃ samantataḥ paśya yodhān raṇe bhinnān dhāvamānāṃs tatas tataḥ
english: "O long-lived one, the Kaurava host is fleeing on every side. Behold the warriors broken in battle, running this way and that.

sanskrit: ete ca sahitāḥ śūrāḥ pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha tvām eva hi jighāṃsantaḥ prādravanti samantataḥ
english: And these heroic Pāñcālas, united with the Pāṇḍavas, seeking to slay you yourself, are rushing forward from all sides.

sanskrit: atra kāryaṃ samādhatsva prāptakālam ariṃdama sthāne vā gamane vāpi dūraṃ yātaś ca sātyakiḥ
english: Determine here what the moment demands, O tamer of foes—whether to stand fast or to advance; for Sātyaki has gone far afield."

sanskrit: tathaivaṃ vadatas tasya bhāradvājasya māriṣa pratyadṛśyata śaineyo nighnan bahuvidhān rathān
english: Even as the son of Bharadvāja was speaking thus, O honored one, the scion of Śini came into view, striking down chariots of every kind.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare yuyudhānena tāvakāḥ yuyudhānarathaṃ tyaktvā droṇānīkāya dudruvuḥ
english: Your men, being slaughtered in battle by Yuyudhāna, abandoned Yuyudhāna's chariot and fled toward Droṇa's division.

sanskrit: yais tu duḥśāsanaḥ sārdhaṃ rathaiḥ pūrvaṃ nyavartata te bhītās tv abhyadhāvanta sarve droṇarathaṃ prati
english: And those chariots with which Duḥśāsana had earlier turned to the fight—all of them, terrified, ran toward Droṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca duḥśāsanarathaṃ dṛṣṭvā samīpe paryavasthitam bhāradvājas tato vākyaṃ duḥśāsanam athābravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing Duḥśāsana's chariot drawn up close at hand, the son of Bharadvāja then spoke these words to Duḥśāsana:

sanskrit: duḥśāsana rathāḥ sarve kasmād ete pravidrutāḥ kaccit kṣemaṃ tu nṛpateḥ kaccij jīvati saindhavaḥ
english: "Duḥśāsana, why have all these chariots fled away? Is it well with the king? Does the lord of the Sindhus yet live?

sanskrit: rājaputro bhavān atra rājabhrātā mahārathaḥ kimarthaṃ dravase yuddhe yauvarājyam avāpya hi
english: You are here a king's son, a king's brother, a great chariot-warrior who has attained the rank of crown prince. Why then do you flee from the battle?

sanskrit: svayaṃ vairaṃ mahat kṛtvā pāñcālaiḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha ekaṃ sātyakim āsādya kathaṃ bhīto 'si saṃyuge
english: Having yourself stirred up this great enmity with the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas, how is it that on meeting Sātyaki alone you are afraid in battle?

sanskrit: na jānīṣe purā tvaṃ tu gṛhṇann akṣān durodare śarā hy ete bhaviṣyanti dāruṇāśīviṣopamāḥ
english: Long ago, while you grasped the dice in the gaming hall, you did not know that these arrows would come to be, cruel as venomous serpents.

sanskrit: apriyāṇāṃ ca vacanaṃ pāṇḍaveṣu viśeṣataḥ draupadyāś ca parikleśas tvanmūlo hy abhavat purā
english: The speaking of harsh words to the Pāṇḍavas in particular, and the affliction of Draupadī—of these you alone were the root, long ago.

sanskrit: kva te mānaś ca darpaś ca kva ca tad vīra garjitam āśīviṣasamān pārthān kopayitvā kva yāsyasi
english: Where now is your pride and your arrogance? Where, O hero, is that roaring of yours? Having enraged the Pārthas, who are like venomous serpents, where will you go?

sanskrit: śocyeyaṃ bhāratī senā rājā caiva suyodhanaḥ yasya tvaṃ karkaśo bhrātā palāyanaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Pitiable is this army of the Bharatas, and pitiable is King Suyodhana, whose hard-hearted brother you are—you who are bent on flight.

sanskrit: nanu nāma tvayā vīra dīryamāṇā bhayārditā svabāhubalam āsthāya rakṣitavyā hy anīkinī sa tvam adya raṇaṃ tyaktvā bhīto harṣayase parān
english: Surely, O hero, this host being torn apart and stricken with fear ought to have been guarded by you, relying on the might of your own arms; yet you this day, forsaking the battle in your terror, gladden the foe.

sanskrit: vidrute tvayi sainyasya nāyake śatrusūdana ko 'nyaḥ sthāsyati saṃgrāme bhīto bhīte vyapāśraye
english: When you, the leader of the host, have fled, O slayer of foes, who else will stand his ground in battle, the fearful taking refuge in one already afraid?

sanskrit: ekena sātvatenādya yudhyamānasya cānagha palāyane tava matiḥ saṃgrāmād dhi pravartate
english: Today, fighting against the Sātvata alone, O blameless one, your mind turns to flight from the battle.

sanskrit: yadā gāṇḍīvadhanvānaṃ bhīmasenaṃ ca kaurava yamau ca yudhi draṣṭāsi tadā tvaṃ kiṃ kariṣyasi
english: When you behold in battle the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, and Bhīmasena, O Kaurava, and the twins, then what will you do?

sanskrit: yudhi phalgunabāṇānāṃ sūryāgnisamatejasām na tulyāḥ sātyakiśarā yeṣāṃ bhītaḥ palāyase
english: Not equal to Phalguna's arrows in battle, whose splendor is like the sun and fire, are these shafts of Sātyaki from which you flee in terror.

sanskrit: yadi tāvat kṛtā buddhiḥ palāyanaparāyaṇā pṛthivī dharmarājasya śamenaiva pradīyatām
english: If indeed your mind is set on flight, then let the earth be given over to the King of Righteousness, and so make peace.

sanskrit: yāvat phalgunanārācā nirmuktoragasaṃnibhāḥ nāviśanti śarīraṃ te tāvat saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: While Phalguna's iron shafts, like serpents loosed from their slough, have not yet entered your body, make your peace with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yāvat te pṛthivīṃ pārthā hatvā bhrātṛśataṃ raṇe nākṣipanti mahātmānas tāvat saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: While the high-souled Pārthas, having slain your hundred brothers in battle, have not yet seized the earth, make your peace with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yāvan na krudhyate rājā dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kṛṣṇaś ca samaraślāghī tāvat saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: While King Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, is not yet wrathful, nor Kṛṣṇa who glories in battle, make your peace with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yāvad bhīmo mahābāhur vigāhya mahatīṃ camūm sodarāṃs te na mṛdnāti tāvat saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: While mighty-armed Bhīma, plunging into the great host, has not yet crushed your own brothers, make your peace with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: pūrvam uktaś ca te bhrātā bhīṣmeṇa sa suyodhanaḥ ajeyāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ saṃkhye saumya saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ na ca tat kṛtavān mandas tava bhrātā suyodhanaḥ
english: Long ago your brother Suyodhana was told by Bhīṣma: 'The Pāṇḍavas are unconquerable in war, O gentle one; make your peace with the Pāṇḍavas.' Yet that dull-witted brother of yours, Suyodhana, did not do so.

sanskrit: sa yuddhe dhṛtim āsthāya yatto yudhyasva pāṇḍavaiḥ gaccha tūrṇaṃ rathenaiva tatra tiṣṭhati sātyakiḥ
english: Now, summoning steadfastness in battle, fight on with effort against the Pāṇḍavas. Go swiftly by chariot to where Sātyaki stands.

sanskrit: tvayā hīnaṃ balaṃ hy etad vidraviṣyati bhārata ātmārthaṃ yodhaya raṇe sātyakiṃ satyavikramam
english: This host, bereft of you, will scatter, O Bhārata. For your own sake, give battle in the field to Sātyaki of true valor."

sanskrit: evam uktas tava suto nābravīt kiṃ cid apy asau śrutaṃ cāśrutavat kṛtvā prāyād yena sa sātyakiḥ
english: Thus addressed, your son answered not a word, but, treating what he had heard as though unheard, set out toward where Sātyaki was.

sanskrit: sainyena mahatā yukto mlecchānām anivartinām āsādya ca raṇe yatto yuyudhānam ayodhayat
english: Joined with a great host of unyielding Mlecchas, and reaching the field, he strove and gave battle to Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: droṇo 'pi rathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pāñcālān pāṇḍavāṃs tathā abhyadravata saṃkruddho javam āsthāya madhyamam
english: Droṇa too, foremost of chariot-warriors, in great wrath rushed upon the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas, holding to a measured speed.

sanskrit: praviśya ca raṇe droṇaḥ pāñcālānāṃ varūthinīm drāvayām āsa yodhān vai śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And entering the array of the Pāñcālas in battle, Droṇa put their warriors to flight by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: tato droṇo mahārāja nāma viśrāvya saṃyuge pāṇḍupāñcālamatsyānāṃ pracakre kadanaṃ mahat
english: Then Droṇa, O great king, proclaiming his name aloud in the battle, wrought a great slaughter among the Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas, and Matsyas.

sanskrit: taṃ jayantam anīkāni bhāradvājaṃ tatas tataḥ pāñcālaputro dyutimān vīraketuḥ samabhyayāt
english: As the son of Bharadvāja was conquering the divisions on every side, the radiant Vīraketu, son of the Pāñcāla king, advanced against him.

sanskrit: sa droṇaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ dhvajam ekena vivyādha sārathiṃ cāsya saptabhiḥ
english: He pierced Droṇa with five arrows of well-smoothed joints, struck his standard with one, and his charioteer with seven.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutaṃ mahārāja dṛṣṭavān asmi saṃyuge yad droṇo rabhasaṃ yuddhe pāñcālyaṃ nābhyavartata
english: There, O great king, I beheld a marvel in the battle: that Droṇa did not at once move against the impetuous Pāñcāla prince in the fight.

sanskrit: saṃniruddhaṃ raṇe droṇaṃ pāñcālā vīkṣya māriṣa āvavruḥ sarvato rājan dharmaputrajayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Seeing Droṇa held in check in the battle, O honored one, the Pāñcālas, desiring the victory of Dharma's son, surrounded him on every side, O king.

sanskrit: te śarair agnisaṃkāśais tomaraiś ca mahādhanaiḥ śastraiś ca vividhai rājan droṇam ekam avākiran
english: With arrows like fire, with costly lances, and with weapons of every kind, O king, they overwhelmed Droṇa alone.

sanskrit: nihatya tān bāṇagaṇān droṇo rājan samantataḥ mahājaladharān vyomni mātariśvā vivān iva
english: Droṇa struck down those swarms of arrows on every side, O king, as the wind sweeping the sky scatters great rain-clouds.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraṃ mahāghoraṃ sūryapāvakasaṃnibham saṃdadhe paravīraghno vīraketurathaṃ prati
english: Then the slayer of enemy heroes fitted to his bow a most dreadful arrow, like the sun and fire, aimed at Vīraketu's chariot.

sanskrit: sa bhittvā tu śaro rājan pāñcālyaṃ kulanandanam abhyagād dharaṇīṃ tūrṇaṃ lohitārdro jvalann iva
english: That arrow, O king, piercing the Pāñcāla prince, the delight of his line, swiftly entered the earth, wet with blood and blazing as it went.

sanskrit: tato 'patad rathāt tūrṇaṃ pāñcālyaḥ kulanandanaḥ parvatāgrād iva mahāṃś campako vāyupīḍitaḥ
english: Then the Pāñcāla prince, the delight of his line, fell swiftly from his chariot, like a great campaka tree from a mountain peak, beaten down by the wind.

sanskrit: tasmin hate maheṣvāse rājaputre mahābale pāñcālās tvaritā droṇaṃ samantāt paryavārayan
english: When that mighty-armed prince, a great archer, was slain, the Pāñcālas in haste surrounded Droṇa on every side.

sanskrit: citraketuḥ sudhanvā ca citravarmā ca bhārata tathā citrarathaś caiva bhrātṛvyasanakarṣitāḥ
english: Citraketu and Sudhanvan, and Citravarman, O Bhārata, and Citraratha as well, racked by grief at their brother's ruin,

sanskrit: abhyadravanta sahitā bhāradvājaṃ yuyutsavaḥ muñcantaḥ śaravarṣāṇi tapānte jaladā iva
english: rushed together upon the son of Bharadvāja, eager to fight, loosing showers of arrows like rain-clouds at the close of the hot season.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno bahudhā rājaputrair mahārathaiḥ vyaśvasūtarathāṃś cakre kumārān kupito raṇe
english: Assailed in many ways by those princely great chariot-warriors, he, enraged in battle, stripped those youths of their horses, charioteers, and cars.

sanskrit: tathāparaiḥ suniśitair bhallais teṣāṃ mahāyaśāḥ puṣpāṇīva vicinvan hi sottamāṅgāny apātayat
english: And with other keen-edged broad arrows, the illustrious one struck down their heads, as though plucking flowers.

sanskrit: te rathebhyo hatāḥ petuḥ kṣitau rājan suvarcasaḥ devāsure purā yuddhe yathā daiteyadānavāḥ
english: Slain, those splendid warriors fell from their chariots to the earth, O king, as the Daiteyas and Dānavas fell of old in the war of the gods and demons.

sanskrit: tān nihatya raṇe rājan bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān kārmukaṃ bhrāmayām āsa hemapṛṣṭhaṃ durāsadam
english: Having slain them in battle, O king, the valiant son of Bharadvāja whirled his unassailable, gold-backed bow.

sanskrit: pāñcālān nihatān dṛṣṭvā devakalpān mahārathān dhṛṣṭadyumno bhṛśaṃ kruddho netrābhyāṃ pātayañ jalam abhyavartata saṃgrāme kruddho droṇarathaṃ prati
english: Seeing the godlike Pāñcāla great chariot-warriors slain, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, exceedingly wrathful, letting tears fall from his eyes, advanced in his fury toward Droṇa's chariot in the battle.

sanskrit: tato hā heti sahasā nādaḥ samabhavan nṛpa pāñcālyena raṇe dṛṣṭvā droṇam āvāritaṃ śaraiḥ
english: Then of a sudden a cry of "Alas! Alas!" arose, O king, when men saw Droṇa hemmed in by the arrows of the Pāñcāla prince in the battle.

sanskrit: saṃchādyamāno bahudhā pārṣatena mahātmanā na vivyathe tato droṇaḥ smayann evānvayudhyata
english: Though covered over in many ways by the high-souled grandson of Pṛṣata, Droṇa did not waver, but fought on, even smiling.

sanskrit: tato droṇaṃ mahārāja pāñcālyaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ ājaghānorasi kruddho navatyā nataparvaṇām
english: Then the Pāñcāla prince, O great king, beside himself with rage, struck Droṇa upon the chest in his wrath with ninety arrows of bent joints.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho balinā bhāradvājo mahāyaśāḥ niṣasāda rathopasthe kaśmalaṃ ca jagāma ha
english: Deeply wounded by that strong warrior, the illustrious son of Bharadvāja sank down upon the floor of his chariot and fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: taṃ vai tathāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ parākramī samutsṛjya dhanus tūrṇam asiṃ jagrāha vīryavān
english: Seeing him brought to such a pass, the valiant, heroic Dhṛṣṭadyumna swiftly cast aside his bow and seized his sword.

sanskrit: avaplutya rathāc cāpi tvaritaḥ sa mahārathaḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ bhāradvājasya māriṣa hartum aicchac chiraḥ kāyāt krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ
english: Leaping down from his chariot, that great warrior in haste swiftly mounted the chariot of the son of Bharadvāja, O honored one, his eyes red with wrath, longing to sever the head from his body.

sanskrit: pratyāśvastas tato droṇo dhanur gṛhya mahābalaḥ śarair vaitastikai rājan nityam āsannayodhibhiḥ yodhayām āsa samare dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ mahāratham
english: Then the mighty Droṇa, recovering, took up his bow and, with span-long arrows ever fit for close fighting, O king, gave battle in the field to the great chariot-warrior Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: te hi vaitastikā nāma śarā āsannayodhinaḥ droṇasya viditā rājan dhṛṣṭadyumnam avākṣipan
english: Those arrows called span-long, made for fighting at close quarters and well known to Droṇa, O king, beat Dhṛṣṭadyumna back.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno bahubhiḥ sāyakais tair mahābalaḥ avaplutya rathāt tūrṇaṃ bhagnavegaḥ parākramī
english: Assailed by those many shafts, that mighty and valiant one, his onset broken, leaped swiftly down from the chariot.

sanskrit: āruhya svarathaṃ vīraḥ pragṛhya ca mahad dhanuḥ vivyādha samare droṇaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ
english: Mounting his own chariot, the hero, the great warrior Dhṛṣṭadyumna, took up his mighty bow and pierced Droṇa in the battle.

sanskrit: tad adbhutaṃ tayor yuddhaṃ bhūtasaṃghā hy apūjayan kṣatriyāś ca mahārāja ye cānye tatra sainikāḥ
english: That marvelous combat between the two the hosts of beings hailed with praise, and the kṣatriyas too, O great king, and whatever other soldiers were there.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ samare droṇo dhṛṣṭadyumnena saṃgataḥ vaśam eṣyati no rājñaḥ pāñcālā iti cukruśuḥ
english: "Droṇa, now joined in combat with Dhṛṣṭadyumna, will surely fall into the power of our king"—so the Pāñcālas cried aloud.

sanskrit: droṇas tu tvarito yuddhe dhṛṣṭadyumnasya sāratheḥ śiraḥ pracyāvayām āsa phalaṃ pakvaṃ taror iva tatas te pradrutā vāhā rājaṃs tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: But Droṇa, swift in battle, struck off the head of Dhṛṣṭadyumna's charioteer, as one knocks a ripe fruit from a tree; and thereupon the horses of that high-souled one bolted away, O king.
